text: The ECB raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, its first increase since 2023. Inflation projections were revised upward while economic growth projections were revised downward. Policymakers cited energy-related inflation pressures and maintained that future rate decisions would remain data dependent. Inflation and growth expectations moved in opposite directions within the forecast framework.

meta.note: Policy direction changed while the future rate path remained explicitly unspecified.

text: U.S. leadership publicly discussed potential seizure or control of Iranian oil infrastructure, including Kharg Island, while additional military action remained active. Negotiations with Iran were simultaneously described as ongoing. Competing control claims persisted regarding energy infrastructure, export flows, and access through the Strait of Hormuz.

meta.note: Military, economic, and territorial control references were presented concurrently without a settled outcome.

text: Producer prices increased 1.1% in May and 6.5% year over year, with energy accounting for the majority of the monthly increase. Core measures rose more slowly than headline wholesale inflation. Producer-price growth exceeded recent consumer-price growth, while expectations for restrictive monetary policy remained broadly intact.

meta.note: Headline and core wholesale inflation measures moved at different rates, with energy contributing most of the observed increase.
